skeleton: dragonfly hovering, seen from above at a slight angle, facing left: root at the thorax (it hovers); body (thorax) with a belly bone carrying its art; head on the thorax with a face carrying the two big round eyes (each a whole eyeball piece), sad brows and the mouth; four wings at their roots under the thorax — wingL/wingL2 the far (left, smaller) fore and hind wings, shaded, wingR/wingR2 the near pair; legs (one piece of three) under the chest; tail in three segments tail → tail2 → tail3, each hinged under the one before so it curls gently.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a friendly dragonfly character, seen from above at a slight angle, facing left. Draw this exact dragonfly as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the thorax: the round turquoise chest with its pale cream front and dark teal spots, as in image 1, alone, without head, wings, legs or tail; its top (normally under the head) and its back end (where the tail joins) rounded off smoothly, with no line across them.
2. the head without its eyes: the round turquoise head with its pale cream lower face, little dark teal spots and the two rosy cheeks, turned to the left as in image 1, with a completely blank face — no eyes, no mouth; the two big round eyes that sit on top of the head in image 1 are left out, the head's top a smooth round line where they would sit.
3. the front part of the tail: the first three turquoise segments of the slim tail, with their dark teal spots, as in image 1; its front end (where it tucks under the thorax) a smooth rounded edge with no line across it; its back end the third segment's own rounded end.
4. the middle part of the tail: the next three turquoise segments, as in image 1; its front end a smooth rounded edge with no line across it, its back end the segment's own rounded end.
5. the tip of the tail: the last three turquoise segments, ending in the rounded tip, as in image 1; its front end a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
6. the upper left wing: the long clear veined wing (pale aqua and cream wash, thin brown outline) that reaches up and to the left behind the head in image 1, drawn whole; its root end, where it joins the body, a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
7. the lower left wing: the long clear veined wing that reaches out to the left in image 1, drawn whole; its root end a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
8. the upper right wing: the long clear veined wing that reaches up and to the right in image 1, drawn whole; its root end a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
9. the lower right wing: the long clear veined wing that reaches out to the right below it in image 1, drawn whole; its root end a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
10. the legs: the three little thin dark turquoise legs dangling below the chest in image 1, side by side as one piece, joined at the top in a small soft rounded patch with no line across it.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge with no line across it. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a friendly dragonfly character; image 2 shows the same dragonfly cut into puppet parts, its head drawn without its two big eyes and with a blank face. Draw the dragonfly's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the dragonfly in image 1, so it fits the head in image 2.

The dragonfly's eyes are two big round bulging eyes on top of its head, each a full round ball with its own brown outline. Every eye piece below is that same big round ball, the same size and round shape; only what is inside it changes.
Draw each piece on its own, spread out in tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching.
Row 1, the left eye (the one on the left in image 1), each with its pupil looking to the left as in image 1:
1. the left eye as it is in image 1: a big round white eye with a large dark brown iris and a white sparkle.
2. the same left eye wide open and surprised: the same big round white eye, its iris a little smaller with more white around it, a white sparkle.
3. the same left eye asleep: the same round ball, its turquoise lid closed over it, a soft downward-curving lash line across it with a few small lashes.
4. the same left eye closed in a happy smile: the same round turquoise ball with a soft shine, an upward-curving closed arc with a few small lashes.
5. the same left eye sad: the same big round white eye, the iris looking down, a soft shine along the bottom, no lid slanting.
6. the same left eye crying: the same round turquoise ball, its lid gently squeezed shut in a soft downward-curving line (a sad closed eye, not a smile), and one small light-blue teardrop just below it.
Row 2, the right eye (the one on the right in image 1), each with its pupil looking to the left as in image 1:
7. the right eye as it is in image 1: a big round white eye with a large dark brown iris and a white sparkle.
8. the same right eye wide open and surprised: the same big round white eye, its iris a little smaller with more white around it, a white sparkle.
9. the same right eye asleep: the same round ball, its turquoise lid closed over it, a soft downward-curving lash line across it with a few small lashes.
10. the same right eye closed in a happy smile: the same round turquoise ball with a soft shine, an upward-curving closed arc with a few small lashes.
11. the same right eye sad: the same big round white eye, the iris looking down, a soft shine along the bottom, no lid slanting.
12. the same right eye crying: the same round turquoise ball, its lid gently squeezed shut in a soft downward-curving line, and one small light-blue teardrop just below it.
Row 3, the mouths and brows:
13. the mouth as it is in image 1: a tiny dark brown smile.
14. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh: smooth and pink inside with a little pink tongue, no teeth at all.
15. the mouth open in a small round 'o', pink inside, no teeth.
16. the mouth in a small sad frown.
17. the left eye's brow, sad: a short thin dark brown line tilted up towards the middle of the face.
18. the right eye's brow, sad: a short thin dark brown line tilted up towards the middle of the face.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the dragonfly flies along to the left, its four clear wings shimmering, then hangs still in the air.
the dragonfly hangs quite still in the air, its wings a shimmering blur, and turns its head to look one way and then the other.

pause.shows: the dragonfly hanging still in the air, its wings a blur, its head turned to look about

animations.description: the dragonfly darts a little way forward in a flash, stops dead in the air, then zips back to where it was.
the dragonfly zigzags along through the air, up and down and up again, then glides back to its spot.
the dragonfly shakes its head no.
the dragonfly looks one way, then the other, then back.
the dragonfly laughs and laughs, bobbing up and down with giggles, its tail wiggling.
the dragonfly cries, head down and tail drooping, its little body shaking with sobs.
the dragonfly gives a big yawn, closes its big round eyes and dozes off, its tail drooping, then wakes up, blinks and smiles.

pause.shows: the dragonfly fast asleep, its big round eyes shut, its tail drooping

animations.description: the dragonfly lifts one big clear wing and waves hello with it.
